newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stock market ends firmer on bank gains.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stock market ends firmer on bank gains.

text.p: Renewed interest in bank shares saw the Nigerian stock trade firmer on Monday and building on last Friday's gains, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 8440.43 from 8437.94 on Friday.
Traders welcomed the trend but said it was too early to predict an end to recent bearish moods.
"The economic situation in the country has not shown any marked improvement although expected increased government spending this month may lift the gloom," said one.
Rising demand for United Bank for Africa shares pushed its share price 20 kobo higher to 12.10 naira.
Wema Bank rose seven kobo to 3.60 naira, International Merchant Bank gained two kobo at 1.54 naira and Owena Bank OWBK.KG added one kobo to 1.37 naira.

First Bank, however, closed at 13.00 naira, down 23 kobo, while Afribank was adjusted for dividend payment and scrip issue. It closed at 3.82 naira, down 2.74 naira. Shares of conglomerates PZ Industries continued to slide on persistent offloading. It fell to 27.00 naira on Monday, shedding 45 kobo.
UAC was down 15 kobo to 16.05 naira.
Cement shares also ended down. Both West African Portland Cement Company and Benue Cement Company slid five kobo each to 61.85 naira and 5.50 naira respectively.
Food firm Nestle was unchanged at 52.30 naira despite announcing a disappointing first quarter result.
It said after-tax profit in the period to end-March 1997 was down to 101.2 million naira from 112.1 million naira in the same 1996 period.
Tire maker Dunlop, whose first quarter account showed a slight improvement, also ended steady at 9.67 naira.
Petroleum marketers African Petroleum and Total TOTL.LG each finished 10 kobo lower, at 55.60 naira and 58.00 naira, respectively.
Traders said investors were still selling the oil shares because of falling profitability.
